meta.title: The Way to Green Hill
meta.textType: functional: written directions on a card

paragraphs: Uncle Dan comes to Green Hill on Sunday. He travels by bus from the town. He does not know the way to the house. Lily is at the house with Grandma and Grandpa. Grandma writes a card with directions. Lily draws a small picture next to each line.

This is the card. "Get off the bus at the post office." "Go straight on along the street, past the fire station." "Turn left at the corner with the big tree." "Walk across the field on the path." "You will see the yellow house with the blue gate on your right." "When it rains, take a taxi."

Lily reads each line out loud to Grandpa. He checks every line. "Which way do you turn at the corner?" asks Grandpa. "You turn left," says Lily. "Uncle Dan should look for the big tree," says Grandpa. "Grandma will wait in front of the house," says Lily. Grandpa takes a photo of the card with his phone. He sends it to Uncle Dan.

On Sunday, Uncle Dan waits at the town bus station. He opens the photo and reads the card. He gets on the bus. He gets off at the post office, by the back exit. He goes straight on along the street, past the fire station. He turns left at the corner with the big tree. He walks across the field on the path. There are three houses, and the yellow house is in the middle. He gets to the house at eleven o'clock. Grandma has tea ready. "Thank you for the card," says Uncle Dan. At the bottom of the card, Lily writes a question for you. "Can you find the yellow house?"
text.summary: Uncle Dan does not know the way to Green Hill. Grandma writes a direction card, Lily draws pictures, and Uncle Dan finds the yellow house.
